purpose: Test whether the exact rank-one Boolean determinant elimination identity extends to constant rank r>=2 with one copy of the current core matrix, constant-size local Schur augmentation, and no duplication of untouched variable state.

model.rank_r_update: M -> M + U V^T, with U,V having r columns.
model.one_core_local_augmentation: N = [[M, U R],[-L V^T, D]], where D,L,R depend only on r (not on M or the remaining variables) and the top-left block contains exactly one copy of M.
model.target_identity: det N = det M + det(M+UV^T) for all invertible M and all U,V, equivalently as a polynomial identity where defined.

theorem.name: RANK_ONE_IS_THE_ONLY_EXACT_ONE_CORE_LOCAL_SCHUR_BOOLEAN_ELIMINATION_CASE_IN_CHARACTERISTIC_ZERO_V0_8
theorem.statement: Over a characteristic-zero field, the target identity in the frozen one-core local augmentation model is impossible for every r>=2. For r=1 it is realized by D=[2], L=R=[1].
proof: Let K=V^T M^{-1}U. Schur complement gives det N = det(M) det(D + L K R).
The matrix determinant lemma gives det(M+UV^T)=det(M) det(I_r+K). Therefore universality requires det(D+LKR)=1+det(I_r+K) for all r by r matrices K.
At K=0, det(D)=2. In characteristic zero D is invertible.
Apply the determinant lemma/Sylvester identity to the auxiliary block: det(D+LKR)=det(D) det(I_r + K R D^{-1} L)=2 det(I_r+K H), with H=R D^{-1}L.
Thus 2 det(I_r+K H)=1+det(I_r+K) for every K.
Compare degree-one coefficients. The right side has linear part tr(K); the left side has 2 tr(KH). Equality for every matrix K forces H=(1/2) I_r.
Compare the degree-r coefficient det(K). The left side contributes 2 det(H) det(K)=2^(1-r) det(K), while the right side contributes 1*det(K).
In characteristic zero 2^(1-r)=1 iff r=1. Hence no r>=2 identity exists in this model.
theorem.positive_control: For r=1, H=1/2 and the concrete block [[M,u],[-v^T,2]] gives det(M)+det(M+uv^T), exactly as v0.7.

algorithmic_consequence.killed: The simplest plan to solve bounded-occurrence SAT by giving each variable a constant-rank determinant update and eliminating variables one by one through a single-core Schur gadget with O(poly(r)) local overhead.
algorithmic_consequence.why_duplication_is_rejected: A generic determinant representation of det(M)+det(M+UV^T) can duplicate M, but doing that once per Boolean variable doubles the representation repeatedly and creates exponential size unless an additional global compression theorem is proved.
survives: nonlocal/global cancellation involving multiple variables at once
augmentations not factoring through the rank-r update subspaces U and V
characteristic-specific mechanisms not covered by the characteristic-zero coefficient argument

next_target.name: E8_MULTI_VARIABLE_GLOBAL_ELIMINATION_WITHOUT_CORE_DUPLICATION_V0_9
next_target.directive: Stop eliminating rank>=2 variables independently. Search for a simultaneous many-variable identity or a different global invariant whose matrix/object grows only polynomially once for the whole formula.
success_obligations: no exponential duplication of the core
